newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower, Dec/March spread widens.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower, Dec/March spread widens.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter futures ended lower in mostly light volume, and the December/March spread widened late, traders said.
Pressure came from a variety of sources. The weekly state crop reports released Monday showed the new wheat crop in generally good shape.
KCBT wheat was also undermined by talk that Argentine wheat could be obtained at the Gulf of Mexico at a cheaper price than U.S. HRW wheat.
But traders said end-of-month short covering helped the market stabilize from its earlier lows.
Support also came from the deliverable HRW wheat stocks in Hutchinson, Kan., which were at 2.4 million bushels on Oct. 25, down from 4.1 million bushels a week earlier.

KCBT wheat closed unchanged to 3-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with Dec down 1-1/4 cents at $4.20. All traded contracts out to May, 1997 set new contract lows, with nearby Dec hitting a new low at $4.18 per bushel.
Traders said Wolcott Lincoln bull-spread 1.5 million Dec/March at 25 to 26 cents. CIS sold 1.6 million Dec and bear-spread 1.5 million March/Dec at 25 to 25-1/2 cents. LFG bought one million March.
The Dec/March inverse traded as wide as 26 cents late, after having traded at 23 cents near the opening.
